pg007_n0007: The digestive system is essential for the health and well-being of the body.
pg007_n0008: In this chapter, you will learn about the concept and parts of the digestive system in human beings.
pg007_n0009: You will also learn about the functions of each part of the digestive system, as well as some disorders in the digestive system and how to prevent them.
pg007_n0010: The competencies developed will enable you to describe how the body obtains nutrients from food.
pg007_n0011: You will also analyse the importance of maintaining a well-functioning digestive system.
pg007_n0015: The importance of the digestive system to human beings.
pg007_n0020: Search for information about the importance of the digestive system in maintaining the well-being of the human body from the library or reliable online resources.
pg007_n0022: Digestion is the biological process by which food is broken down into smaller particles which provide nutrients that can be absorbed by the body.
pg007_n0023: These nutrients are used by the body for growth, repair, production of energy and protection against diseases.
pg007_n0024: For the body to obtain these nutrients, food must be broken down into small particles that can be absorbed by the body.
pg007_n0025: Digestion takes place within the digestive system.
pg007_n0027: The digestive system is a collection of organs that are responsible for breaking down food into small particles and absorbing nutrients into the body.
pg008_n0002: It is important to eat a balanced diet, drink sufficient amount of water and avoid foods high in fat or sugar to keep the digestive system healthy.
pg008_n0003: Apart from human beings, other animals also have digestive systems suited to the type of food they eat.

pg008_n0024: The digestive system consists of various organs that work together to facilitate the breakdown of food.
pg008_n0025: The human digestive system begins in the mouth and ends at the anus.
pg008_n0026: It includes the digestive tract, organs and glands that work together.
pg008_n0027: The main parts of the digestive tract are the mouth cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine and large intestine, as shown in the Figure.
pg008_n0028: The small intestine consists of the duodenum and ileum, while the large intestine includes the colon, rectum and anus.
pg008_n0029: The organs that make up the digestive system include the tongue, liver, pancreas and gallbladder.
pg008_n0030: The digestive system is also composed of salivary and gastric or stomach glands.
pg008_n0031: Other organs of the digestive system such as the liver, pancreas and gallbladder, also contain glands that produce digestive enzymes which break down food.
pg009_n0017: The digestion process starts in the mouth cavity, where food is chewed using teeth and mixed with saliva.
pg009_n0018: The digestion of foods rich in starch begins in the mouth cavity and are thereafter transported through the oesophagus into the stomach.
pg009_n0022: The pharynx is the part of the digestive system located between the mouth and the oesophagus.
pg009_n0023: Its function is to direct food from the mouth cavity to the oesophagus.
pg009_n0024: A flap called epiglottis prevents food from entering the airway by closing the windpipe during swallowing.
pg009_n0028: The oesophagus is a muscular tube that connects the pharynx to the upper part of the stomach.
pg009_n0029: Food moves through the oesophagus in a series of muscle contractions and relaxations in the walls.
pg009_n0030: This movement helps to move food to the stomach.
pg009_n0034: Upon reaching the stomach, food is broken down with the help of acid and digestive enzymes, which are produced there.

pg010_n0003: The chyme then moves to the small intestine for further digestion and absorption.
pg010_n0007: This part is located between the stomach and the large intestine.
pg010_n0008: The first part of the small intestine, where digestion occurs, is called the duodenum.
pg010_n0009: The duodenum receives enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the gallbladder which breaks down food.
pg010_n0010: The main foods broken down in this part are fats, proteins and carbohydrates.
pg010_n0012: The ileum is the last part of the small intestine where the digestion process is completed.
pg010_n0013: When partially digested food reaches the ileum, it stimulates the intestinal walls to release digestive enzymes.
pg010_n0014: These enzymes complete the breakdown of proteins, carbohydrates and fats.
pg010_n0015: The small intestine then absorbs nutrients from digested food and allows the body to utilize them for various bodily functions.
pg010_n0019: The large intestine is located after the small intestine.
pg010_n0020: Its function is to absorb water and minerals from undigested food into the body.
pg010_n0021: It also uses the remaining undigested food to form faeces which are then eliminated from the body.
pg010_n0022: Also, it contains beneficial bacteria that help to break down food remains and produce certain vitamins.
pg010_n0023: The colon, rectum and anus are parts of the large intestine.
pg010_n0027: This is the first part of the large intestine responsible for reabsorption of water from the digested food into the body.
pg010_n0028: It is also the section where some nutrients, such as vitamins, are produced by bacteria found in this part.
pg010_n0029: The colon also serves to store faeces before they are eliminated from the body.
pg010_n0033: The rectum is the second part of the large intestine, where faeces are stored temporarily before being expelled from the body during defecation.
pg010_n0034: It controls the removal of the faeces from the body.

pg012_n0002: The digestive system can be affected by various disorders that can lower its efficiency in food digestion or nutrient absorption.
pg012_n0003: A digestive system disorder is a condition that affects the normal functioning of the digestive tract, making it difficult for the body to properly digest and/or absorb food.
pg012_n0004: These disorders can be congenital, inherited or caused by lifestyle factors and poor nutrition.
pg012_n0005: Some of the disorders in the digestive system include:
pg012_n0009: This is a disorder of the digestive system that causes a person to have difficulty in passing faeces or to have hard, dry faeces.
pg012_n0010: This problem can be caused by eating foods with low fibre content, not drinking enough water, and lack of physical exercises.
pg012_n0011: In addition, health issues such as poor functioning of the large intestine can also cause constipation.
pg012_n0015: Constipation can be prevented by eating foods rich in fibre such as fruits and vegetables, drinking enough water and carrying out physical exercises regularly.
pg012_n0019: This is a condition where the stomach feels full, tight or swollen, often due to a building up of gas in the stomach.
pg012_n0020: It can result from overeating, eating too fast, food intolerance or consuming gas-producing foods.
pg012_n0021: Symptoms of bloating include stomach pain, a feeling of fullness and burping.
pg012_n0022: Sometimes, the gas can have a strong, unpleasant odour.
pg012_n0026: To prevent bloating, it is important to eat food in moderate amounts and chew it slowly to reduce the amount of swallowed air.
pg012_n0027: Also, drink enough water to aid digestion in the stomach.
pg012_n0028: Limit intake of gas-producing foods such as beans and carbonated beverages.
pg012_n0029: Eating fibre-rich fruits and vegetables also prevent bloating.
pg012_n0033: This is a condition that occurs when acid from the stomach rises into the oesophagus, causing pain or a burning sensation in the throat.
pg012_n0034: Symptoms of heartburn include a burning feeling in the chest, frequent burping and a sour taste in the mouth.
pg012_n0035: Heartburn can be caused by overeating.
pg012_n0036: It can also be caused by eating foods with high amount of spices or fats.
pg013_n0002: These foods take longer to be digested and can increase stomach acid production.
pg013_n0003: Another cause of heartburn is eating large amounts of acidic foods, such as lemons and limes.
pg013_n0004: Beverages like soda, coffee and alcohol can also cause heartburn.
pg013_n0005: Eating just before sleeping can also lead to heartburn.
pg013_n0009: Heartburn can be prevented by eating slowly, allowing the digestive process to occur effectively.
pg013_n0010: Also, eating smaller amounts of food more frequently and avoiding foods that cause heartburn.
pg013_n0011: High intake of acidic foods, such as oranges, lime, tangerine, potatoes, beans and tomatoes, and foods with a lot of spices or fat should be avoided.
pg013_n0012: After eating, rest for two to three hours before lying down or going to bed.
pg013_n0013: Additionally, exercise or strenuous activity shortly after eating should be avoided.
pg013_n0014: If heartburn persists, it is advisable to seek medical advice.
pg013_n0018: This is a condition resulting from erosion of the lining of the stomach wall.
pg013_n0019: Stomach ulcers can be caused by eating foods that are high in acid or having a bacterial infection that erodes the walls of the stomach lining.
pg013_n0020: Sometimes, stomach ulcers can be caused by prolonged periods of hunger.
pg013_n0021: When the acid and enzymes in the stomach come into contact with the eroded walls, they cause sores.
pg013_n0022: This is because acid burns the stomach wall, creating ulcers or sores.
pg013_n0023: Stomach ulcers cause severe pain in the abdomen.
pg013_n0024: When the ulcers are large, they may cause heavy bleeding.
pg013_n0025: Symptoms of stomach ulcers include intense pain, such as a burning sensation in the stomach.
pg013_n0026: Other symptoms include vomiting blood and passing stool mixed with blood.
pg013_n0030: Stomach ulcers can be prevented by eating at regular intervals and reducing the intake of highly acidic foods.
pg013_n0031: Additionally, avoiding smoking and alcohol can help to prevent ulcers.
pg013_n0035: Maintaining proper eating habits is important for good health and for preventing problems in the digestive system.

pg014_n0004: It is also important to have regular mealtimes and reduce the intake of unhealthy foods and snacks that lack essential nutrients.
pg014_n0006: It is advisable to consume whole grains and drink sufficient amounts of water to ensure proper functioning of the digestive system.
pg014_n0007: Drinking water, half an hour before and after a meal is important for effective digestion and nutrient absorption.
pg014_n0008: You can improve your body health and protect yourself from disorders in the digestive system by following these habits.

pg017_n0004: Growth and development in plants and animals
pg017_n0008: Growth is among the characteristics of living things.
pg017_n0009: Plants and animals pass through different stages of growth before reaching adult stage.
pg017_n0010: In this chapter, you will learn about the concept of growth and development in plants and animals.
pg017_n0011: You will also learn about the essential requirements for plant and animal growth and development.
pg017_n0012: Additionally, you will explore the different stages of plant and human growth and development, along with the changes that occur at each stage.

pg017_n0018: Essential requirements for plant and animal growth.
pg017_n0020: Concept of plant and animal growth and development
pg017_n0024: Search for information about the concept of growth in plants and animals from the library or reliable online resources.
pg017_n0026: Growth in living things is the increase in body size (height and width) and weight.
pg017_n0027: It is an irreversible change that occurs in plants and animals as a result of cell division, cell elongation and cell differentiation.
pg017_n0028: Plant growth involves the increase in height of a plant, which occurs at the tips of roots and shoots.
pg017_n0029: Also, plants grow by increasing the width or thickness of the plant stem.
pg017_n0030: Like plants, animals also grow by increasing in height and weight.
pg017_n0031: Plants and animals grow through different stages.
pg017_n0032: The changes through which plants and animals undergo throughout their life cycle are called development.
pg017_n0033: In plants, development involves germination, occurrence of new leaves, roots and other parts such as flowers, and
pg018_n0003: Development in animals includes changes in body structure and functions.
pg018_n0004: Examples of development in animals include a caterpillar becoming a butterfly and a baby growing into an adult.
pg018_n0005: Development in plants and animals involves physical and behavioral changes.
pg018_n0009: Plant growth and development refers to the series of changes a plant undergoes throughout its life cycle.
pg018_n0010: Plant growth and development involves different stages.
pg018_n0011: Each stage of development plays a vital role and has distinct features.
pg018_n0012: These stages include seed germination, seedling, vegetative stage, reproduction stage, and senescence.
pg018_n0015: Figure 1: Stages of plant growth and development
pg018_n0019: Seed germination is the process by which a seed develops into a new plant.
pg018_n0020: A seed germinates when it has matured and has received the required conditions, which are sunlight, water, air, nutrient and optimum temperature.
pg018_n0021: During germination, the radicle emerges and anchors the seedling into the soil.
pg018_n0022: The radicle also absorbs water and nutrients needed for plant growth.
pg018_n0023: The radicle is the embryonic root of the plant.
pg018_n0024: Another part called the plumule also emerge, it is the embryonic shoot of the plant.
pg018_n0025: It begins to grow upwards, eventually forming the stem and leaves of the plant.
pg018_n0026: During this stage, food stored in the seed is used as a source of energy for germination.
pg019_n0004: Seedling is the stage that follows after seed germination.
pg019_n0005: At this stage, the seedling develops few leaves.
pg019_n0006: Its roots continue to grow into the soil to absorb water and nutrients.
pg019_n0007: During this stage food storage is minimal, hence the seedling begins to manufacture its own food through photosynthesis.
pg019_n0011: In this stage, the plant continues to grow and develops more leaves.
pg019_n0012: It increases the production of its own food through photosynthesis.
pg019_n0013: The roots, stems and branches continue to grow and become strong.
pg019_n0017: This is the stage whereby the plant matures and develops from the vegetative stage to the reproductive stage.
pg019_n0018: During this stage, flowering plants begin to form buds, which gradually develop into flowers that contain reproductive structures.
pg019_n0019: Flowers facilitate pollination and fertilisation, leading to the formation of fruits or seeds.
pg019_n0020: Fruits contain seeds for growing new plants.
pg019_n0021: Plants such as watermelon, orange, tomato, avocado, maize and bean produce seed-bearing fruits.
pg019_n0022: Some plants do not form flowers but produce seeds, which may germinate into new plants.
pg019_n0026: Senescence is the natural process of aging in plants, during which cell division stops making the tissues, or whole organs gradually lose their function and eventually die.
pg019_n0027: Senescence of different plant parts such as leaves and flowers occurs throughout the plant life, although its rate increases as the plant gets older or after producing seeds.
pg019_n0028: However, unlike in annual plants, in perennial plants senescence occurs in specific organs like leaves and flowers, allowing the plant to survive and grow for many years.

pg021_n0002: Plant growth depends on the availability of essential requirements including sunlight, air, water, nutrients, and optimum temperature to grow well.
pg021_n0003: The absence of any of these requirements can affect plant growth.
pg021_n0004: For example, a plant may receive enough sunlight, but if it lacks water or sufficient nutrients, its growth will be affected.
pg021_n0005: The essential requirements for plant growth are as follows:
pg021_n0009: Sunlight helps plants to grow by providing both light and heat energy.
pg021_n0010: Plants use light energy to make their own food.
pg021_n0011: Plant leaves contain a green pigment called chlorophyll, that absorbs sunlight and enables plants to make their own food through photosynthesis.
pg021_n0012: Without adequate light, plants cannot grow well due to a lack of food.
pg021_n0016: Plants use carbon dioxide gas to make their own food through the photosynthesis process.
pg021_n0017: Carbon dioxide gas enters the plant through small openings on the leaves called stomata.
pg021_n0018: The stomata open to allow carbon dioxide gas to enter, enabling photosynthesis to take place.
pg021_n0019: Insufficient amount of carbon dioxide reduces the ability of the plant to produce its own food.
pg021_n0020: Plants also need oxygen for their growth.
pg021_n0021: Oxygen helps to burn food to produce the energy required for plant growth.

pg027_n0029: Stages of human growth and development
pg027_n0031: Humans pass through different stages of growth and development, including infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age (Elderliness).
pg027_n0032: Each stage has unique changes that contribute to overall growth and development in humans.
pg027_n0037: This is the first stage of growth and development of a human being.
pg027_n0038: Infancy stage covers the range of the period from birth to two (2) years.
pg027_n0039: This is the time after the baby is born and starts early learning.
pg027_n0040: During this period, a baby learns things like touch, movement and emotion.
pg027_n0041: Eventually, the baby is able to hold their head up, sit down, crawl, roll, walk a few steps without support and develops milk teeth.
pg027_n0042: By the time a baby reaches two years of age, they can run and climb up and down without support.
pg028_n0002: sounds are observed during this period.
pg028_n0003: A baby can also show anger, happiness, sadness and fear.
pg028_n0004: Also, a baby learns how to recognise people around them and those who take care of them.
pg028_n0008: The childhood period ranges from the age of 2 years to 13 years.
pg028_n0009: During this period, a child increases in height and weight, hence, a lot of changes in the body occur.
pg028_n0010: During this stage the milk teeth are replaced by permanent teeth.
pg028_n0011: The child develops skills in climbing, jumping, riding, running, self-feeding, drawing and colouring.
pg028_n0012: The child learns social roles like dressing, eating and bathing on their own.
pg028_n0013: During this period, the development of a child’s skills with the help of parents or guardians is very important.
pg028_n0014: Interactions among children themselves and their parents or adults are also important.
pg028_n0015: Children need to be provided with a balanced diet, a conducive environment for playing, proper health services, regular cleanliness, shelter and clothing.
pg028_n0019: Adolescence is a transition stage between childhood and adulthood.
pg028_n0020: It is during this stage that puberty occurs.
pg028_n0021: Puberty is defined as the phase where a child’s physical and sexual characteristics start to mature into adult features.
pg028_n0022: A child also undergoes physical, mental and emotional changes which are driven by hormones.
pg028_n0023: Puberty usually starts between the ages of 12 to 13 years in boys and 11 to 12 years in girls, though it can vary due to genetic, nutritional and environmental factors.
pg028_n0027: Both boys and girls undergo various changes during puberty.
pg028_n0029: (a) Physical changes during puberty in girls

pg029_n0009: Physical changes in girls during puberty include:
pg029_n0022: Growth of hair under the armpits and around the pubic area.
pg029_n0031: Appearance of pimples/acne on the face in some girls.
pg029_n0037: Maturation of eggs and the beginning of menstruation.
pg029_n0041: Menstruation is a natural biological process of discharging blood mixed with mucus from the break down of lining of the uterus through the vagina.
pg029_n0042: The onset of menstruation is a key sign of puberty in girls.
pg029_n0043: Menstruation usually occurs once every month forming a part of the menstrual cycle in which one or more eggs mature.
pg030_n0002: The menstrual cycle refers to the period from the first day of menstruation to the day before the next period.
pg030_n0003: It usually lasts 28 days as shown in Figure 7.
pg030_n0004: However, some women have cycles that range between 21 to 35 days.
pg030_n0010: Menstrual bleeding occurs when the uterine lining, which was built to prepare the uterus to receive a fertilised egg sheds off.
pg030_n0011: The duration of menstruation varies from person to person.
pg030_n0012: Typically, menstruation lasts between 3 to 5 days, though some women may have shorter periods, while others may experience longer periods of up to 7 days.
pg030_n0013: During menstruation special materials called sanitary pads or sanitary napkins are used to absorb the blood that comes through the vagina.
pg030_n0014: It is advised to use cotton-made pads.
pg030_n0015: Pads are attached to the inside of underwear with adhesive strips or wings.
pg030_n0016: It should be changed regularly typically after every 3 to 4 hours, in order to maintain hygiene and prevent effects that can rise like rashes or infections.

pg030_n0023: Sometimes, irregularities or disorders occur in the menstrual cycle.
pg030_n0024: Some of these irregularities include discomfort during menstruation, lack of menstruation periods, severe menstrual pain, and prolonged or excessive bleeding during the menstruation period.
pg030_n0025: These conditions may be caused by hormonal changes, stress, or underlying health issues.
pg031_n0002: Discomfort during menstruation: Some women experience discomfort during menstruation, making it difficult for them to perform their daily activities efficiently.
pg031_n0003: The discomfort may last a few hours or several days, depending on the person.
pg031_n0004: The symptoms may include depression, stomach pain, headaches, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, loss of appetite, and water retention in the feet, hands and fingers.
pg031_n0005: To reduce the discomfort, it is advised to take physical exercises 3 to 5 times a week, eat a balanced diet and get enough sleep and rest.
pg031_n0007: Severe menstrual pain: Some women experience severe pain during menstruation.
pg031_n0008: The pain may begin at puberty or later in life.
pg031_n0009: The pain is often caused by uterine contractions due to hormonal imbalance.
pg031_n0010: Other causes include infections in the cervix, uterine fibroids, and infections within the reproductive system.
pg031_n0011: Any woman can experience pain during menstruation, however, those who smoke, consume alcohol, are overweight, or have experienced early puberty before age 11 are often at higher risk.
pg031_n0013: Excessive menstrual bleeding: Excessive menstrual bleeding occurs when a woman loses more blood than usual or has a longer menstruation period.
pg031_n0014: This may result from a blood clotting disorder that prevents proper clotting of blood or hormonal imbalances that affect the menstrual cycle.

pg032_n0015: During puberty, boys and girls experience the following social changes:
pg032_n0017: (a) Self-awareness: During puberty, adolescents begin to explore and understand themselves better, recognising their identity as boys or girls and developing emotional connections.
pg033_n0004: Desire for recognition: Adolescents at this stage seek recognition for their roles in society and the world.
pg033_n0005: This desire is influenced by gender, peer groups, culture and family expectations.
pg033_n0008: Desire for freedom: At this age, adolescents want to make their own decisions without interference from parents or guardians.
pg033_n0009: This often leads to conflicts between them and their parents or guardians.
pg033_n0010: While parents have a responsibility to guide their children, adolescents must also recognise the role of their parents and practise responsible freedom.
pg033_n0013: Curiosity to learn new things: During puberty, boys and girls become curious and eager to try new experiences.
pg033_n0014: This curiosity can sometimes lead to risky behaviours.
pg033_n0015: For example, they may want to learn skills such as driving cars and riding motorcycles.
pg033_n0016: Some may start smoking or abusing drugs.
pg033_n0017: This urge can also lead to early sexual activity, which may result in unintended pregnancies or sexually transmitted infections like HIV.
pg033_n0021: During puberty, boys and girls experience mental changes that influence their behaviour.
pg033_n0026: Increased ability to understand reality in their surroundings.
pg033_n0029: Improved problem-solving skills, even for complex and confusing issues.
pg033_n0032: Enhanced ability to understand other people’s thoughts and perspectives.
pg033_n0035: Ignoring the consequences of some of their actions.
pg033_n0039: During puberty, boys and girls also show changes in their interactions with society, such as:
pg033_n0043: Spending more time with friends than family: At this stage, adolescents feel that friends are more important than family.
pg033_n0044: They believe that, peers understand them better because they share similar thoughts.
pg033_n0045: As a result, they prefer spending more time with friends instead of family.
pg033_n0048: Developing different opinions from adults: Adolescents start forming their own opinions and questioning what they see or hear.
pg034_n0002: They feel confident in making decisions based on their beliefs.
pg034_n0003: This can cause conflicts with parents, guardians, or older relatives.
pg034_n0004: However, these disagreements are normal and do not harm family relationships.
pg034_n0007: Desire to compete: Adolescents enjoy competing and comparing themselves with their peers in different aspects of life.
pg034_n0008: They strive to be the best in everything they do, both at home and outside, and they want to be seen as role models.
pg034_n0012: Adolescents experience significant emotional changes during puberty, including:
pg034_n0015: Intense and fluctuating emotions: During puberty, emotions change quickly.
pg034_n0016: A small event can make a teenager very happy, angry, or excited.
pg034_n0017: They may cry or feel frustrated over minor issues.
pg034_n0018: This is normal because their brain is still learning to manage emotions.
pg034_n0019: If family and society do not understand this, conflicts may occur.
pg034_n0022: Increased self-consciousness: Teenagers become highly aware of how they appear to others.
pg034_n0023: They care about their physical appearance and fashion choices.
pg034_n0024: They often compare their bodies to their peers or celebrities.
pg034_n0025: This is why many teenagers imitate the dressing styles, hairstyles, speaking and even walking styles of famous people they admire.
pg034_n0027: Ways to cope with changes during puberty
pg034_n0030: Observe the challenges that boys and girls face during puberty in your community.
pg034_n0031: Then, suggest ways to manage them.
pg034_n0033: The changes during puberty in boys and girls cannot be avoided.
pg034_n0034: However, following some strategies can help to reduce the challenges of these changes.
pg034_n0035: To manage puberty effectively, the following are recommended:
pg034_n0037: Engaging in physical exercises: During puberty, adolescents grow quickly, gain weight, and develop more strength.
pg034_n0038: Exercises improve blood circulation, keep the body active, reduce stress and promote happiness.
pg034_n0040: Getting sufficient sleep and eating a balanced diet: Sufficient sleep is essential for a growing body.
pg034_n0041: It helps relieve tiredness and regulate
pg035_n0003: A balanced diet with essential nutrients supports healthy physical and mental development.
pg035_n0005: Avoiding alcohol, tobacco, and other substances: These substances affect the nervous system and impair decision-making abilities.
pg035_n0006: Since puberty comes with challenges in making the right choices, avoiding substances and maintaining a healthy lifestyle is crucial.
pg035_n0007: Respecting others also promotes good morals.
pg035_n0009: Sharing challenges with friends or family: Every adolescent experiences puberty differently.
pg035_n0010: Sometimes, young people think they are the only ones facing these changes, leading to emotional distress, anxiety, and low self-esteem.
pg035_n0011: Talking to others helps in getting the right guidance and support.
pg035_n0013: Seeking help from trusted individuals: Adolescents may face difficulties they cannot handle alone.
pg035_n0014: It is important to seek advice from trusted people such as parents, guardians, teachers and other reliable adults.
pg035_n0016: Maintaining personal hygiene: Personal hygiene is crucial during puberty.
pg035_n0017: This includes bathing regularly, washing clothes, ironing and keeping hair neat.
pg035_n0018: For girls, changing sanitary pads or menstrual products in time during menstruation is essential for hygiene and comfort.
pg035_n0022: Adulthood is a stage where physical growth slows down or stops, and the body focuses more on maintaining overall health rather than increasing in size.
pg035_n0023: During this period, the rate of growth is minimal.
pg035_n0024: This occurs in the age range of 18 - 65 years.
pg035_n0025: This is the period when human beings mature with full physical and intellectual maturity.
pg035_n0026: A person in this stage is self-confident and is more likely to make sound decisions and take responsibility.
pg035_n0027: An adult person requires proper nutrition and should engage in regular physical exercises.
pg035_n0031: Old age occurs normally at the age of 65 years and above.
pg035_n0032: This is the period when the body systems and muscles become weak in comparison to those in the younger stages.
pg035_n0033: Physical body strength decreases, body hair becomes grey and vision and hearing ability decrease.
pg035_n0034: Skin loses elasticity and a person experiences loss of memory.
pg035_n0035: Elderly people require maintaining personal hygiene, eating a balanced diet and taking light physical exercises.
pg035_n0036: Also, doing regular health checkups is important to maintain a good health status.

pg038_n0017: The concept of the reproductive system

pg038_n0023: Reproduction is a biological process by which living organisms give rise to offspring.
pg038_n0024: Reproduction ensures an increase in number of living things, and continuity of the species from one generation to another.
pg038_n0025: There are two types of reproduction, namely, sexual and asexual reproduction.
pg038_n0026: Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of reproductive cells (sperm and egg) to form an offspring.
pg038_n0027: In humans and some plants, the reproductive cells are produced by two parents (male and female parents).
pg038_n0028: However, in some flowering plants, only one parent can produce both male and female reproductive cells.
pg038_n0029: In contrast, asexual reproduction involves only
pg039_n0002: one parent without the need for fusion of the reproductive cells.
pg039_n0003: Asexual reproduction produces offspring that are genetically identical to the parent.
pg039_n0005: Reproduction in humans biengs as in other organisms, occurs through the reproductive system.
pg039_n0006: The reproductive system is a collection of organs and structures in living organisms responsible for the production of offspring.
pg039_n0007: In humans beings, this system is divided into the male and female reproductive systems.
pg039_n0008: Each system has specialised organs that work together to enable reproduction.
pg039_n0009: Reproduction in humans is possible only after puberty.
pg039_n0010: The reproduction in humans involves the production of reproductive or sex cells called gametes.
pg039_n0011: The male gametes are called sperm and are produced in the testes, while the female gametes are called ova or eggs, are produced in the ovaries.
pg039_n0013: Hormones, such as oestrogen, progesterone, and testosterone regulate the reproductive system.
pg039_n0014: They control the growth of reproductive organs, the menstrual cycle, the production of gametes, and pregnancy.
pg039_n0016: The reproduction in human beings is important because it leads to an increase in population size.
pg039_n0017: Therefore, it helps to ensure the continuity of generations.
pg039_n0018: It allows them to pass on their traits and contribute to the ongoing existence of their kind.
pg039_n0019: This is because reproduction involves the transfer of genetic materials from one generation to the next.

pg045_n0008: Disorders in the reproductive system are various conditions that interfere with or impair the normal functioning of the reproductive system.
pg045_n0009: These disorders can be structural or health related.
pg045_n0010: The causes of disorders may include genetic inheritance, unhealthy lifestyle factors, poor nutrition, chronic diseases, or environmental influences, such as exposure to harmful chemicals or radiation.
pg045_n0011: However, regular medical check-ups and early treatment can help prevent or correct reproductive system disorders in both males and females.
pg045_n0013: Disorders in the male reproductive system
pg045_n0015: Disorders in the male reproductive system refer to conditions that can interfere with the normal functioning of the male reproductive system.
pg045_n0020: This is a condition in which a male is unable to impregnate a female.
pg045_n0021: Male infertility can be caused by various factors, including producing too few sperm resulting in reduced chances of fertilisation.
pg045_n0022: It can also result from weak sperm that are unable to swim toward the egg.
pg045_n0023: Additionally, sperm abnormalities such as missing tails, having two tails, lacking head, or having an irregular shape can contribute to infertility.
pg045_n0025: Furthermore, the testes may fail to produce sperm due to diseases, poor nutrition or hormonal deficiencies.
pg045_n0026: Another cause of infertility is blocked sperm ducts often resulting from sexually transmitted infections such as gonorrhoea and syphilis.

pg045_n0031: This disorder can affect both the urinary and reproductive systems.
pg045_n0032: Prostate enlargement may result from infections or cancer, causing blockage of the urethra leading to difficulty in urination.
pg046_n0002: Disorders in the female reproductive system
pg046_n0004: These are conditions that interfere with the normal functioning of the female reproductive system.
pg046_n0009: Infertility is the condition whereby the female egg cannot be fertilised.
pg046_n0010: Infertility in women can be caused by various factors, including failure of eggs to mature.
pg046_n0011: This condition often results from hormonal imbalances whereby the ovaries may fail to produce sufficient oestrogen or progesterone.
pg046_n0013: Infertility in females may also be caused by sexually transmitted infections such as gonorrhoea, syphilis, and chlamydia.
pg046_n0014: These infections can block the fallopian tubes, hence preventing the egg from passing through to allow fertilisation.
pg046_n0018: The cervix can be damaged due to complications during childbirth or due to infections within the cervix.
pg046_n0019: This may result in a deformed cervix.

pg046_n0024: They include amenorrhea, which is a condition in which a matured female stops having her periods or misses them for a certain period of time without being pregnant.
pg046_n0025: Menstrual disorders also include painful periods due cramps of the uterine wall, a condition termed as dysmenorrhea.
pg046_n0026: They can also include excessively heavy or prolonged menstrual flow, a condition known as menorrhagia.
pg046_n0027: These disorders may be caused by hormonal imbalances, particularly lack of oestrogen, genetic abnormalities, chronic illnesses, and stress.
pg046_n0028: These disorders can be treated, hence, it is important to seek medical advice.

pg047_n0003: Therefore, it is important to care for it to prevent problems that can reduce its efficiency.
pg047_n0004: Some of these problems include infections that can cause diseases in the reproductive parts.
pg047_n0005: Examples of diseases that affect the reproductive organs include sexually transmitted diseases and other infections from fungi, bacteria or other germs.
pg047_n0006: The following should be done to care for the reproductive system:
pg047_n0010: It is important to keep our bodies clean by taking a bath with clean water and soap every day.
pg047_n0011: It is also important to clean the genital parts with clean water after using the toilet.
pg047_n0012: It is recommended to use a clean toilet and observe cleanliness in the toilet.
pg047_n0013: Also, wear clean and dry underwear every day, and never share underwear with anyone else to avoid infections.
pg047_n0015: Eating a balanced diet and taking regular physical exercises
pg047_n0017: Eating a balanced diet and drinking enough water helps to keep your body and reproductive system healthy.
pg047_n0018: Also, taking physical exercise regularly helps to make the body stronger and keeps the reproductive system healthy.
pg047_n0019: It also helps to prevent excessive weight gain, which can harm the body and the reproductive system.
pg047_n0023: Some habits are dangerous to our body health.
pg047_n0024: Using alcohol, cigarettes, and other harmful drugs can damage the body and reproductive system.
pg047_n0025: It is best to avoid such habits to maintain a healthy reproductive system.

pg073_n0003: Consider the following tasks in a game:
pg073_n0007: Moving a sprite to a location ten steps to the right.
pg073_n0010: Moving a sprite to the right until it reaches the edge.
pg073_n0013: Playing a sound while the game is playing.
pg073_n0015: All of these tasks require an action to be performed repeatedly before the final result can be obtained.
pg073_n0016: To perform the first task, the sprite moves one step to the right (repeat this ten times) until it reaches the desired location.
pg073_n0017: In the second task, the sprite moves to the right until it reaches the edge.
pg073_n0018: In the third task, the action repeated is play a sound.
pg073_n0019: The sprite plays the desired sound repeatedly until the game ends.
pg073_n0020: So, as long as the game is playing, the sound will play.
pg073_n0022: Notice that in the first task, the action is repeated a fixed number of times (ten times).
pg073_n0023: In the second task, the action is repeated until a given condition is met (reaching the edge).
pg073_n0024: On the other hand, in the third task, the action of playing a sound is repeated continuously until the game stops.
pg073_n0026: This means there are three kinds of repetition control structures, namely repeat ( ) loop, repeat until ( ) loop and forever loop.
pg073_n0027: For the repeat ( ) loop, the value in the brackets represents the number of times to repeat an action.
pg073_n0028: For the repeat until loop, the value in the brackets represents the condition that makes the loop stop.
pg073_n0029: The forever loop will run continuously until either you manually stop the program or use the stop block.
pg073_n0030: In Scratch, these loops can be found in the Control block menu (see Figure 6).

pg073_n0034: The repeat ( ) loop is used when you want to do an action a certain number of times.
pg073_n0035: The repeat until ( ) loop is used when you want to do an action until a certain condition is met.
pg073_n0036: The forever loop is used when you want to do an action without stopping.
